text:
morgan: quick sync — we need to pick a default for shared-service edge: proto/gRPC across internal services with an HTTP/JSON gateway, or REST-first (JSON) with optional proto for high-throughput paths?
priya: i'm leaning gRPC everywhere. smaller wire, enforced schema, easier migration for streaming calls. main worry is browser clients and some platform tooling.
alex: +1 for gRPC for service-to-service. but gateway complexity goes up. our console and some infra expect JSON now.
dan: if we do gRPC-first we need a clear gateway contract (headers, error translation, quota propagation). that’s the hard part.
serena: quota propagation is what kills us in previous rollouts — requests hitting the edge lost tenant headers and quota numbers got double-counted. need an invariant: X-Tenant-ID and X-Quota-Token must be forwarded unchanged or rejected.
morgan: agreed. can we define a tiny header shim that every gateway must support? like `x-rw-tenant`, `x-rw-quota` and a checksum header `x-rw-signature` to prevent accidental rewrites?
priya: signature seems heavy. maybe just require `x-rw-tenant` + `x-rw-origin` and a route-level config to enforce immutability. gateway returns 400 if headers missing.
alex: +1 for fail-fast. also telemetry needs to correlate trace ids across gateway and backend. we should standardize `x-rw-trace` and surface it in console.
dan: telemetry aside, fallback behavior matters — if gRPC endpoint is overloaded, gateway should fallback to a compatible REST variant (losing streaming). we need model compatibility rules.
serena: that implies we maintain two surface variants for some services. cost of maintaining parity is real. can we instead have single model and translation layer? (proto -> json)
priya: runtime transcoding works but there's edge cases (any/oneof fields, binary blobs). we must define canonical wire for those.
morgan: proposal: default internal surface = proto/gRPC. Gateway does HTTP JSON transcoding for external clients. For critical high-throughput routes we provide native gRPC pass-through via edge (no transcoding). Gateways must implement header immutability checks and quota header passthrough.
alex: sounds practical. how about rollouts? we need canary telemetry metrics that show quota delta, latency, and token loss across gateway vs service. console needs a per-route panel.
dan: instrument points: edge ingress, gateway-transcode, service ingress, quota-eval. add counters: quota-unmatched, header-drop, transcoding-errors. emit as tags: route, env, canary-id.
serena: echoing dan — also log size of JSON after transcoding; we've seen explosion in tokens when proto repeated fields map to JSON. that bubbled up token costs in inference services before.
priya: UX for devs: allow service teams to opt-out of transcoding per-route via a `rw.allow_transcode: false` annotation in proto options or OpenAPI extension. Default = true.
morgan: example annotation snippet:```proto
// service.proto
option (rw.service_options) = { allow_transcode: false };
``` 
alex: +1. also let's add a lightweight lint in CI that flags routes missing header invariants or missing telemetry spans.
dan: for quota propagation, gateway should attach a `x-rw-quota-signature` computed by signing tenant+route with gateway key so backend can verify the header wasn't spoofed. makes the earlier signature idea more concrete.
priya: ok that solves trust. key rotation? gateway exposes JWKS endpoint and services fetch key cache.
morgan: ops-bot, can you note a checklist for rollout phasing?
ops-bot: checklist created: phase-0 define headers + telemetry tags; phase-1 implement gateway header enforcement; phase-2 add transcoding configs + opt-out; phase-3 canary (5% traffic) with telemetry dashboard; phase-4 broader rollout and key rotation plan.
serena: for canary signals, console dashboard should show: header-drop rate, quota-reconcile delta, transcoding-error rate, 95p latency, and token-size inflation. make thresholds configurable.
alex: also emit a `rw.rollout` tag so we can slice metrics by rollout id (canary-123). UI needs quick toggle to drill into affected tenants.
dan: one more: fallback policy semantics. prefer `fallback: rest-compat` (downgrade to JSON) or `fallback: reject` (return 503). default = rest-compat. team can set route-level policy.
morgan: agreed. i'll draft a short RFC and include the header names, JWKS flow, telemetry counters, and a sample gateway config block. anyone want to add final bits?
priya: add migration step for browser clients: recommend using gRPC-web via envoy or keep JSON clients hitting gateway. document pros/cons.
serena: add a short script to validate `x-rw-quota-signature` in go and python for service teams.
ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-05-03T02:00:00Z if RFC approved.
morgan: thanks all — i'll open RFC and link here. :thumbsup:
__notes: messages are a single continuous Slack thread string; timestamps are unix seconds; no title field per agents.md
